reading: Each grey (5) piece at the bottom is translated (no rotation) up into the top red wall so that it exactly plugs a matching hole, and is recoloured blue (1); its original position is cleared.

slots.pieces: the grey 8-connected objects in the lower part
slots.holes: background notches in the red wall touching its open side
slots.match: piece placed where its top cells fill a hole exactly (shape match, same orientation)
slots.rest: red wall kept, original piece cells cleared

why: every hole of the wall is filled exactly by one piece of identical shape; piece cell count is preserved

reading: Cut out the red square outline; inside it, draw the small 3x3 coloured shape scaled up by (interior size / 3) so it exactly fills the interior.

slots.frame: the red (2) square outline object, output is its bounding box
slots.shape: the other small object's 3x3 bounding box
slots.placement: scaled shape fills the frame interior exactly

why: output equals the outline box with the interior equal to the shape upscaled by an integer factor

reading: Every 3x3 hollow square of blue (1) is replaced by a red (2) plus sign in the same 3x3 box; all other objects stay.

new_rows.name: ring_tl
new_rows.datalog:
nfg(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- px(Y, X, 0), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
ring_tl(Y2, X2) :- nfg(Y, X, N), N = 8, Y2 = Y - 1, X2 = X - 1.

why: the unit is the constant 3x3 patch [020,222,020] (zeros written) placed with its top-left at the top-left of each hollow 3x3 ring (a background cell with all 8 neighbours filled)

reading: Each 4-connected piece of 4 or more cells falls straight down until it touches the bottom edge; pieces of 3 or fewer cells (short lines, single cells, the small L) stay where they are.

new_rows.name: heavy
new_rows.datalog:
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
adj(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X, cell(Y2, X2, C).
reach(Y, X, Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
reach(Y, X, Y3, X3) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), adj(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
csize(Y, X, count(Y2, X2)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2).
heavy(Y, X) :- csize(Y, X, N), N > 3.

why: each heavy piece keeps its shape and column and ends with its lowest row on the bottom border (downward direction); light pieces unchanged

reading: Find the 3x3 squares that are entirely background (0) in the noisy grid and paint them blue (1); when two such squares overlap, only the first in reading order is painted.

new_rows.name: empty3
new_rows.datalog:
nbg(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- px(Y, X, 0), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, 0).
ctr(Y, X) :- nbg(Y, X, N), N = 8.
blocked(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y2, X2), Y2 < Y, D = Y - Y2, D < 3, E = X - X2, E < 3, F = X2 - X, F < 3.
blocked(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), ctr(Y, X2), X2 < X, E = X - X2, E < 3.
keep(Y, X) :- ctr(Y, X), !blocked(Y, X).
empty3(Y, X) :- keep(Y, X).
empty3(Y2, X2) :- keep(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.

why: every cell of each selected all-zero 3x3 square becomes 1; nothing else changes (the third pair has two overlapping candidates, only the upper-left one is filled)

reading: The grid is a 3x3 array of 3x3 panels split by grey lines. The panel containing a yellow (4) cell is copied into the panel whose index equals the 4's position inside its own panel; every other panel is cleared, separators kept.

slots.panels: the 9 cells of the 3x3 panel layout cut by grey (5) separators
slots.target: panel at (row, col) = position of the 4 within the source panel
slots.rest: all other panels cleared to 0; separators kept

why: output has exactly one non-empty panel, equal to the input's 4-panel, at the index given by the 4's local position

reading: A big chevron shape sits above scattered single dots. In each column where a dot lies below the chevron, a line of the dot colour is drawn from just under the chevron's lowest cell in that column down to the bottom edge.

new_rows.name: under_arch
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dot(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 1.
arch(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N > 1.
under_arch(Y, X) :- dot(Y, X), arch(Y2, X), Y2 < Y.

why: each line runs vertically through a dot below the arch, upward until the arch (first obstacle) and downward to the bottom border; dots not under the arch, or above it, draw nothing

reading: Count the distinct colours of the 3x3 input: one colour gives a grey (5) top row, two colours give the grey main diagonal, three colours give the grey anti-diagonal; everything else becomes 0.

slots.count: number of distinct colours in the input
slots.pattern: 1 -> top row, 2 -> main diagonal (top-left to bottom-right), 3 -> anti-diagonal

why: output is one of three fixed 3x3 patterns chosen only by the input's colour count

reading: Each L-tromino (three cells of a 2x2 box) shoots a diagonal ray of its colour out of its missing corner: the corner cell stays empty and the ray starts one step beyond it, continuing to the grid edge.

new_rows.name: notch
new_rows.datalog: notch(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X, C), cell(Y, X2, C), cell(Y2, X2, C).

why: the ray lies on the diagonal through the L's filled corner and its empty corner, pointing away from the L, coloured like the L, from the cell after the notch to the border

reading: The output doubles the width: the input is kept and a horizontally mirrored copy with colours inverted (0 becomes 8, 2 becomes 0) is attached on the side whose edge the red shape touches.

slots.side: the copy goes on the side (left/right) where the red shape touches the grid edge

why: output = input beside its inverted mirror, mirrored about the edge column the shape touches
